directAnswer: Pope Clement IX was Giulio Rospigliosi of Pistoia, a diplomat and opera librettist who reigned from 1667 to 1669. He helped mediate the Peace of Aachen in 1668, arranged a temporary settlement with the Jansenists, and commissioned Bernini's angels for the Ponte Sant'Angelo; the fall of Candia to the Ottomans is said to have hastened his death.

paras: Giulio Rospigliosi was born in Pistoia on 28 January 1600 and studied with the Jesuits and at Pisa. In Rome he became a literary figure in the Barberini circle and wrote librettos for early operas, including Sant'Alessio and Chi soffre speri, often counted among the first comic operas.
He served as nuncio to Spain for nearly ten years and then as secretary of state under Alexander VII, who made him a cardinal in 1657. He was elected on 20 June 1667.

sections.h2: Peace of Aachen and the Clementine Peace
paras: Clement IX worked to restore good relations with France and Spain. His diplomacy helped bring about the Peace of Aachen in 1668, ending the War of Devolution between Louis XIV and Spain.

He also arranged the so-called Clementine Peace of 1668 and 1669, under which four French bishops who had resisted the anti-Jansenist formulary signed it with a respectful silence on certain points. The compromise brought a decade of calm to the dispute.

sections.h2: Charity, Saints, and the Angels of Ponte Sant'Angelo
paras: Clement IX lived modestly, gave generously to the poor, and avoided enriching his family; his reported motto described him as clement to others but not to himself. He beatified Rose of Lima in 1668 and canonized Peter of Alcantara and Mary Magdalene de' Pazzi in 1669.

He commissioned Bernini and his workshop to create the ten marble angels bearing the instruments of the Passion that line the Ponte Sant'Angelo, installed around the end of his reign and early in his successor's.

Clement IX sent money and ships to help Venice defend Candia, on Crete, which the Ottomans had besieged for more than twenty years. A French expedition he encouraged failed, and Candia surrendered in September 1669.
Contemporaries believed the loss broke his health. He died on 9 December 1669 and is buried in St. Mary Major.

keyFacts: Born Giulio Rospigliosi in Pistoia on 28 January 1600
Wrote opera librettos, including Chi soffre speri
Helped mediate the Peace of Aachen (1668)
Arranged the Clementine Peace with French Jansenist bishops
Died 9 December 1669; buried in St. Mary Major

faqs.question: Was Clement IX really an opera writer?
faqs.answer: Yes. Before his election, Giulio Rospigliosi wrote librettos for Roman operas in the 1630s and 1640s, including Chi soffre speri, considered one of the earliest comic operas.

faqs.question: Who commissioned the angels on Ponte Sant'Angelo?
faqs.answer: Clement IX commissioned Bernini's workshop to carve the ten angels holding instruments of the Passion. They were installed around 1669 to 1671.

faqs.question: What was the Clementine Peace?
faqs.answer: A 1668 to 1669 compromise in which French bishops sympathetic to Jansenism signed the required formulary, ending open conflict over Jansenism for about a decade.
